capability_investigated:
WhisperProcessor feature extractor framing (fixed 30s mel window) and the
batch interface of frozen.asr_backend.generate — it accepts an (N, n_mels,
n_frames) StorageView with a list of N prompts and returns N results.
what_i_learned:
The extractor pads/truncates any input to exactly one 30s window, so the
stub silently dropped everything after 0:30 of each call (structural
deletion, length_ratio floored). generate() is batched over the leading
axis, so multiple 30s windows can be decoded in one call and concatenated.
hypothesis:
Split the waveform into consecutive non-overlapping 30s windows, extract mel
features per window, decode them all in one batched generate() call, and join
the per-window text in order. This recovers the deleted tail — the dominant
error axis for multi-minute 0715 calls — without touching decode params.

capability_investigated:
GPU memory behavior of frozen.asr_backend.generate when fed an
(N, n_mels, n_frames) batch — the OOM crash from iter_001's all-windows-in-
one-call batch on multi-minute 0715 calls.
what_i_learned:
The batched generate() over the leading axis allocates decode state for all
N windows at once on a float16 CUDA model; long calls (many 30s windows)
exceed GPU memory and raise "CUDA failed with error out of memory". Peak
memory scales with batch size, so decoding windows sequentially (batch=1)
keeps the structural-deletion fix while staying within VRAM.
hypothesis:
Keep the 30s windowing that recovers the truncated tail, but iterate windows
one at a time through generate() and concatenate the per-window text. This
removes the OOM crash while preserving the length-ratio recovery.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s **decoding_kwargs surface — specifically the beam-search and
anti-repetition knobs the frozen docstring advertises (beam_size, patience,
repetition_penalty) plus no_repeat_ngram_size, none of which the parent
pipeline uses (it decodes pure-greedy beam_size=1, temp=0.0).
what_i_learned:
The parent's per-window deletion is not purely structural windowing loss:
4/12 files carry the repeated_text flag (repeated 0.27) while length_ratio
sits at 0.65. That is the classic greedy long-form Whisper failure — the
decoder enters a repetition loop, spends the per-window token budget on a
repeated run, and the collapsed run reads as deletion. So the repetition
axis and the coverage axis share one cause, addressable purely through
decode params with no new mechanism.
hypothesis:
Replace greedy decode with beam_size=5 + patience=1.0 to stop premature
collapse, and add repetition_penalty=1.15 + no_repeat_ngram_size=3 to break
loops before they consume the budget. This should raise length_ratio and
cut the repeated_text rate, lowering corpus_cer. Cost ~5x inference
(105s parent → ~525s) stays under the 719.9s budget.

capability_investigated:
The prompt-token side of generate()'s decode path — specifically the
<|notimestamps|> special token that every prior iteration pinned in the
forced prompt, and the alternative timestamp-decoding regime that omitting it
unlocks (the decoder then emits <|t|> segment-boundary tokens in the returned
sequences_ids). Never used in the ledger, which only covered mel framing,
batched-OOM, and beam/repetition decode kwargs.
what_i_learned:
Coverage loss is not just blind 30s cutting — in <|notimestamps|> greedy mode
large-v3 emits EOT early within a window on dense multi-utterance audio,
transcribing only the front and stopping, which is exactly the length_ratio
0.65 / deletion-80% signature. The frozen surface lets me switch to the
trained timestamp regime purely by dropping <|notimestamps|> from the forced
prompt; the returned sequences_ids then carry timestamp tokens (every id >=
<|0.00|>) which I filter out before tokenizer.decode so they don't pollute
text. Stride stays fixed 30s, so decode-call count and runtime are unchanged.
hypothesis:
Decoding each 30s window in timestamp mode (prompt without <|notimestamps|>)
keeps the model transcribing to the window end instead of terminating early,
raising length_ratio and cutting the dominant deletion axis without adding
windows or risking the runtime budget. Timestamp tokens are stripped from
sequences_ids before text decode.

capability_investigated:
The numeric value of the timestamp tokens in generate()'s returned
sequences_ids — not their presence (family_003 already established that
dropping <|notimestamps|> makes them appear), but that each id decodes to a
wall-clock offset via (id - timestamp_begin) * 0.02, letting me locate where
each emitted segment sits inside the 30s window.
what_i_learned:
family_003's hallucination regression (0.091 -> 0.182) rides on the feature
extractor's silent padding of the final short window: in timestamp mode
large-v3 keeps emitting <|t|> segments past the real audio and invents text
for the padding. The timestamp values family_003 discarded are exactly the
signal to gate that — a segment whose start offset >= len(chunk)/sr is
padding-region and can be dropped, with full 30s windows unaffected.
hypothesis:
Keep timestamp decoding (family_003 coverage) but parse segment boundaries
and keep only text whose segment starts before real_seconds = len(chunk)/sr,
composing family_003's length_ratio win with family_001's lower hallucination
instead of trading one for the other.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s returned timestamp tokens used as a SEEK-FEEDBACK signal, not
just text/padding filtering. Prior iters (004/005) established that dropping
<|notimestamps|> makes <|t|> tokens appear and that their offset is
(id - timestamp_begin) * 0.02. This iter investigates using the LAST emitted
segment's end offset to set the next window's start, replacing the fixed 30s
stride — the standard long-form Whisper seek loop, never driven before.
what_i_learned:
The best's length_ratio 0.74 is structurally explained by fixed striding:
in timestamp mode large-v3 still EOTs partway through a 30s window (~22s on
dense audio), and a fixed 30s stride permanently skips the un-transcribed
~8s tail of every window (22/30 ≈ 0.73 ≈ observed 0.74). The decoder stamps
where it actually stopped via the last timestamp token, so that stop point
is recoverable as a seek target rather than a silent loss.
hypothesis:
Advancing seek to the last segment's end offset (floored at 20s to bound
window-count/runtime) re-reads the skipped tail in the next window, lifting
length_ratio toward 1.0 and cutting the dominant deletion (76%) without a
new decode regime — purely by closing the gap fixed striding bakes in.

capability_investigated:
The advance-clamp expression in the adaptive seek loop and the numeric range
of generate()'s returned timestamp tokens — specifically the upper bound of
(ts_tokens[-1] - timestamp_begin)*0.02*sr that the parent wraps in
min(max(advance, min_advance), window).
what_i_learned:
The Whisper timestamp vocabulary spans only <|0.00|> through <|30.00|> within
a single 30s window, so the largest possible last-timestamp offset is exactly
30.0s = _WINDOW_SECONDS. Therefore advance = (id - begin)*0.02*sr is bounded
above by `window` by construction, and the outer min(..., window) clamp is
dead code that can never bind. The min_advance floor is the only load-bearing
guard (it prevents a near-zero advance from blowing up the decode-call count).
hypothesis:
Ablate the redundant upper clamp: replace min(max(advance, min_advance),
window) with max(advance, min_advance). This removes a guard that provably
never fires, simplifying the seek loop with zero behavioral change, so CER
stays at the parent's 0.2095 while the pipeline is leaner and clearer.

capability_investigated:
The previous-text-conditioning path of generate()'s prompt argument — the
decode call accepts arbitrary leading token ids, not just the SOT triple, and
Whisper was trained with a <|startofprev|> prefix carrying prior-window text
as long-form context. Every prior iter built the prompt purely from
<|sot|><|ko|><|transcribe|>, so this input was never exercised.
what_i_learned:
The forced prompt has a second, unused segment: a <|startofprev|>-led prefix
of raw text token ids placed BEFORE <|startoftranscript|>. The tokenizer
exposes <|startofprev|> via convert_tokens_to_ids, and the decode call passes
whatever id list it is given straight through, so prior-window text can be fed
back as context. Decoder context is 448 tokens, so the prefix must be capped
(~half) to avoid starving the current window's emission.
hypothesis:
Prepend the previous window's text_ids (capped at 200) behind <|startofprev|>
to each window's prompt. With coverage already at 0.92 the dominant residual
is 45% substitution; lexical carry-over across the adaptive-seek boundary
should stabilize recurring proper nouns and insurance-domain terms and reduce
boundary substitution, without changing the seek loop or runtime.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_scores flag (the per-sequence length-normalized avg
log-prob it hands back, discarded every prior iter) and the
sampling_temperature / sampling_topk sampling path — never exercised since
the loop always decoded pure greedy (beam_size=1, temp=0.0, default topk=1).
what_i_learned:
generate() exposes two unused returns/controls that together implement
Whisper temperature fallback: result.scores[0] (only populated when
return_scores=True) gives a length-normalized avg log-prob usable as a
confidence gate, and sampling_temperature only takes effect when
sampling_topk != 1 (with the default topk=1 the decoder is argmax and
temperature is inert), so the fallback path must set sampling_topk=0 to
actually sample the full distribution and escape a greedy repetition loop.
hypothesis:
iter_003 established the residual coverage/deletion loss shares a cause with
greedy repetition loops (collapsed run reads as deletion). So decode greedy
first, then re-decode only degenerate windows (zlib compression_ratio > 2.4
OR avg_logprob < -1.0) at escalating temperature with topk=0 sampling. Clean
windows pay nothing; degenerate ones get a non-greedy retry instead of
poisoning both the text and the timestamp seek target.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam-search controls (beam_size, length_penalty) on the
adaptive-seek parent. length_penalty was discoverable in the frozen
docstring but never load-bearing because the loop always decoded greedy
(beam_size=1), under which CT2's length normalization exponent is inert.
what_i_learned:
length_penalty is a no-op at beam_size=1 (greedy emits a single hypothesis,
so there is no length-normalized re-ranking to bias). It only becomes a
coverage lever once beam_size>1, at which point the CT2 score is divided by
((5+len)/6)^length_penalty, so length_penalty>1 favors longer hypotheses —
the direct decode-side counter to the dominant deletion axis. Beam search
also gives a margin against the greedy repetition loop that collapses the
one repeated_text file into apparent deletion.
hypothesis:
Switch the per-window decode from beam_size=1 to beam_size=3 with
length_penalty=1.1, keeping temperature 0.0. The longer-hypothesis bias
should lift length_ratio above the stalled 0.92 and recover deletion, while
beam_size=3 (not 5) bounds the ~3x decode cost under the 719.9s budget
(parent inference was 142.6s).

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_no_speech_prob flag and the result.no_speech_prob field
it populates — the decoder's trained probability that a window contains no
speech, derived from the <|nospeech|> logit at the first decode step. The
frozen docstring advertises this return but every prior iter discarded it
(the ledger covers mel framing, batched-OOM, beam/repetition kwargs,
timestamp tokens, startofprev conditioning, and return_scores/sampling — never
the no-speech probability).
what_i_learned:
Setting return_no_speech_prob=True makes generate() attach a per-window
no_speech_prob to each result alongside sequences_ids, independent of beam
search. This is the trained gate for the silence-window hallucination the
per-file diagnosis exposes: files carrying hallucination_hits have very deep
silence floors (rms_db_p05 −72 to −82 dB) and long silent runs, so a 30s
window landing in dead air has high no_speech_prob yet still emits invented
domain text — that fabrication is what shows up as substitution/insertion and
also corrupts the adaptive-seek timestamp. The signal lets that window be
dropped without touching real-speech windows (which score low).
hypothesis:
Read result.no_speech_prob each window; when it exceeds 0.8 (set high, not
Whisper's 0.6, to protect the now-healthy length_ratio 0.93), discard the
window's text and skip a full window past it instead of trusting its
fabricated last-timestamp. This removes the silent-window hallucination that
feeds the dominant substitution axis while leaving genuine coverage intact.
